title: Queries for Number of Palindromes
statementMd:
You've got a string $*s* = *s*_{1}*s*_{2}... *s*_{|*s*|}$ of length $|*s*|$, consisting of lowercase English letters. There also are $*q*$ queries, each query is described by two integers $*l*_{*i*}, *r*_{*i*}$ $(1 ≤ *l*_{*i*} ≤ *r*_{*i*} ≤ |*s*|)$. The answer to the query is the number of substrings of string $*s*[*l*_{*i*}... *r*_{*i*}]$, which are palindromes.

String $*s*[*l*... *r*] = *s*_{*l*}*s*_{*l* + 1}... *s*_{*r*}$ $(1 ≤ *l* ≤ *r* ≤ |*s*|)$ is a *substring* of string $*s* = *s*_{1}*s*_{2}... *s*_{|*s*|}$.

String $*t*$ is called a *palindrome*, if it reads the same from left to right and from right to left. Formally, if $*t* = *t*_{1}*t*_{2}... *t*_{|*t*|} = *t*_{|*t*|}*t*_{|*t*| - 1}... *t*_{1}$.

## Input

The first line contains string $*s*$ $(1 ≤ |*s*| ≤ 5000)$. The second line contains a single integer $*q*$ $(1 ≤ *q* ≤ 10^{6})$ — the number of queries. Next $*q*$ lines contain the queries. The $*i*$-th of these lines contains two space-separated integers $*l*_{*i*}, *r*_{*i*}$ $(1 ≤ *l*_{*i*} ≤ *r*_{*i*} ≤ |*s*|)$ — the description of the $*i*$-th query.

It is guaranteed that the given string consists only of lowercase English letters.

## Output

Print $*q*$ integers — the answers to the queries. Print the answers in the order, in which the queries are given in the input. Separate the printed numbers by whitespaces.

## Note

Consider the fourth query in the first test case. String $*s*[4... 6]$ = «`aba`». Its palindrome substrings are: «`a`», «`b`», «`a`», «`aba`».
